name: Native desktop shell wrapping the web client
best: teams: Cleanest thin-shell split at scale: native code owns windows, tray, toasts, updates, media and crash recovery while the whole UI stays a web client; it detects a missing/old WebView and has a web fallback. buzz-product-162 (Tauri 2, Rust-owned state) is the closest stack fit for Verevon; qm-architecture-112 is the most locked-down minimal variant.
mechanism: Shell process loads the remote web app (or a bundled copy) in a system WebView; renderer is sandboxed (no Node, contextIsolation), gets a narrow typed bridge; native side owns tray/badge/notifications/deep links/updates. Tauri 2 equivalent: tauri plugins single-instance, deep-link, window-state, updater, notification, global-shortcut; Rust commands as the bridge; CSP locked to the gateway origin.

verevon.gap: Verevon v3 is a web SPA only; no Electron/Tauri/MSIX package. No tray, native notifications, protocol handler or OS presence.

benefit: Teams/Slack-grade presence: Space messages and agent completions reach the user when the tab is closed; tray showing running agents; protocol links from email/Office. Keeps all authority in the gateway (shell is just another same-origin client).
approach: Phase 1 = installable PWA (see Multi-surface cluster) to get most of the value cheaply. Phase 2 = Tauri 2 shell (Rust, matches gateway stack) loading the gateway origin, no local tokens (reuse BFF cookie in an isolated partition), narrow command set (notify, badge, open-external, deep-link). Owned by Frontend Plane.
risks: Signing/notarisation and update infrastructure cost; a second client to test; must not cache Space content locally in ways that break ZDR (no offline message store without retention policy).
rationale: All five references ship one, but Verevon can capture most of the user-visible value (notifications, install, badge) with a PWA first; a native shell becomes necessary for tray/global hotkeys/quick composer.

name: Narrow, typed and validated web-to-native bridge
best: teams: PIE is a uniform versioned RPC (invokables, host events, host-initiated calls, sync calls, batching) over a capability-per-module catalog (53 namespaces); Slack adds per-channel Joi schemas with validation-failure beacons (slack-product-surface-146) and qm adds sender/frame/origin checks (qm-architecture-115).
mechanism: Single message envelope {messageName, messageId, isInvokable, args}; each namespace registers methods with a schema; host validates sender origin + schema, rejects and reports drift; web-defined state passes as opaque blobs so schema changes do not need a native release. In Tauri: one #[tauri::command] per capability with serde-validated args + capability ACL file; reject unknown origins.

verevon.gap: No native shell, so no bridge. (Verevon's typed ActionDescriptor/zod action contract is the analogous pattern on the web side.)

benefit: If a shell is built, a narrow validated bridge keeps the authority model intact: the web app cannot escalate to OS powers beyond an allowlist.
approach: Define the bridge as a versioned schema in packages/ (shared TS + Rust serde types), ≤15 commands initially; sender-origin check to the gateway origin; telemetry on validation failures.
risks: Bridge sprawl (Slack 122 channels, Teams ~545 methods) increases attack surface; keep it minimal.
rationale: Only relevant together with the desktop shell; when built it is a security requirement, not an option.

name: OS protocol handler with single-instance link forwarding
best: slack: One documented grammar (channel, open, app, setting, login-v2, magic-login) registered on Win32, MSIX and macOS with a single-instance lock and a protocol-activation sanity check; buzz adds a de-duplicated cold-start pending queue (buzz-architecture-095).
mechanism: Register scheme; requestSingleInstanceLock; second-instance/open-url events push the URL into a queue that drains once the renderer reports ready; parser maps cmd+params to typed routes with allowlists. PWA alternative: manifest protocol_handlers ("web+verevon") mapped to /open?u=%s.

verevon.gap: Only HTTPS routes (/spaces/:spaceId + hash tabs). No custom scheme, no PWA protocol_handlers, so links from mail/Office/other apps always open a browser tab.
verevon.strengths: HTTPS deep links already work everywhere a browser does.

benefit: Links to a Space, message or agent run open in the installed app instead of a new tab; needed for Teams-like "chat with" actions.
approach: Interim: PWA protocol_handlers + URL handling on the gateway origin. With the Tauri shell: deep-link plugin + cold-start queue; parse into the same typed route table as the SPA router.
risks: Link parsing is an injection surface; allowlist commands and never execute actions from a link without user confirmation.
rationale: Table-stakes for native clients, but meaningless until Verevon is installable; low effort once it is.

name: Entity deep-link routing and URL-synced view state
best: teams: Toast clicks, deep links and lifecycle events are normalised into one (entity, action) command the web UI executes (q5). Slack-shell-and-native-005 adds mapping the team in a link to a workspace the user actually belongs to and holding links until the web app has loaded; qm-product-124 pages older history until a ?seq= target message is present and highlights it.
mechanism: Route table: entity types (space, thread, message, agent, run, task) x actions (open, reply, join); resolver checks membership before navigation (fails closed with an explanation); message links load the transcript window around the target id and scroll/highlight; notifications reuse the same command.

verevon.gap: Space + tab are linkable (hash tabs), but no code was found for message/thread permalinks, agent-run links inside a Space, or a single command router shared with notifications (grep for permalink/?message=/messageId= found nothing). Notification click-through path should be verified.
verevon.strengths: Clean /spaces/:spaceId routes with hash tabs and roving tablist.

benefit: Humans and agents can cite exact messages, decisions and runs ("see this run"), which is how cooperation is coordinated in Slack/Teams; agents can post links that humans open in-place.
approach: Add /spaces/:spaceId/m/:messageId and /spaces/:spaceId/runs/:runId routes in the Solid router; Application Plane projection exposes a "window around message id" read; resolver asks the gateway for access (never widens owner-plane ACL); notifications emit the same route objects.
risks: Links must not leak titles/previews to non-members (unfurl only after an ACL check); ZDR Spaces must not keep resolvable message ids beyond retention.
rationale: Message/run permalinks are a daily collaboration primitive in every reference; Verevon already has the routing base so the gap is small and very visible.

name: Auto-update with release channels and safe install timing
best: slack: Server decides whether a client should update (should-i-update with platform, version, channel, installer type), hourly checks, and update-failure attribution via the expected next version (q5). grokbot-agent-product-104 adds the agent-specific rule: never install while an agent is working, install while the user is away. Teams-shell-and-native-003 updates web assets separately from the native shell.
mechanism: State machine idle -> checking -> staging -> ready; feed URL from track+version+platform; 204 = none; signed artifacts; apply on idle/quit; block while calls/uploads/agent runs are active; record expected version to classify a crash-on-launch as update failure.

verevon.gap: No desktop client. For the web SPA, deploys replace the bundle but open tabs keep the old one (see Client version gating).
verevon.strengths: Web deploys give instant updates without installer infrastructure.

benefit: Required once a shell exists; the agent-aware "do not restart while an agent is running" rule matters for long agent runs streamed into a Space.
approach: tauri-plugin-updater with a gateway-served manifest (server decides per org/channel), stable/beta tracks, idle install, block while a run is streaming in the window.
risks: Broken update channel strands users; needs rollback.
rationale: Mandatory part of the shell, not independent value.

name: Client version gating: minimum versions, staleness nags, update-required hints
best: grokbot: Per-feature minimum client versions with a machine-readable update-required hint the UI can act on (SRC q4); Teams documents a staged nag-then-block policy (DOC only).
mechanism: Remote config {min_version, feature_min_versions, max_age_days}; API responses carry CLIENT_UPDATE_REQUIRED when a stale client calls a feature; UI shows a reload/update banner.

verevon.gap: No build id/version is exposed to the client (grep for buildId/__APP_VERSION__/version.json found nothing), so a tab open across a deploy keeps running the old bundle against a newer gateway contract with no "new version, reload" prompt; lazy-chunk 404s after deploy are not handled (no root error boundary).

benefit: Prevents subtle breakage when gateway/Space contracts change (Space event schemas, action registry ids) while users keep long-lived Space tabs open; essential for a realtime workroom left open all day.
approach: Gateway adds an X-Verevon-Client-Min header and /version endpoint; Vite injects the build id; the SPA compares on visibility change and SSE reconnect, shows a non-blocking reload banner, and forces reload on contract-version mismatch.
risks: Forced reloads during typing lose drafts; persist composer drafts first.
rationale: Cheap and prevents a real class of production bugs for long-lived realtime tabs.

name: Signed packaging, multi-format distribution and release engineering
best: buzz: Immutable release candidates where PR merge is the authorization event, signed canary then promote, separate desktop/relay/mobile lanes; Slack (slack-shell-and-native-039) covers the widest format matrix; Teams declares capabilities explicitly in the manifest.
mechanism: One deterministic candidate commit per release; CI builds signed artifacts per OS/arch (MSIX/MSI/DMG/AppImage); canary channel, then promote; installer type reported in the user agent so the update service can branch.

verevon.gap: No desktop artifacts; web deploy only (Dockerfile, nginx).
verevon.strengths: Single web deploy pipeline is simpler.

benefit: Prerequisite for enterprise desktop rollout (MSI/MSIX for IT).
approach: Tauri bundler for MSIX/MSI + DMG; reuse buzz's candidate-PR pattern in CoresSystem CI.
risks: Code-signing certificate custody.
rationale: Only after the shell decision; part of its cost.

name: Feature flags, remote config, preview rings and experiments
best: teams: Layered providers resolved by ring, tenant and account with local override and an editor page (q5), plus user-facing Labs/Insider/Public preview programmes; grokbot-agent-product-109 shows typed dynamic configs with fallback values and validators (e.g. group-chat discouragement policy).
mechanism: Config service returns typed values per (org, ring, user); client caches with fallbacks and validators; preview programme = per-org/per-user ring; feature descriptions shown in a Labs panel.

verevon.gap: Only plan entitlement booleans (feature_flags in the billing payload) were found; no remote-config/ring system, no user-facing preview programme, no per-org staged rollout of Space/agent features. Verify Control Plane for an org feature-flag service.
verevon.strengths: Entitlements come from the Control Plane rather than client constants.

benefit: Staged rollout of new agent capabilities per org (and kill switches) reduces risk of agent misbehaviour in shared Spaces; a Labs opt-in suits an AI-first product.
approach: Control Plane owns a typed flag/ring registry per org (audited), exposed through the gateway navbar/bootstrap payload; Model Plane reads the same flags for agent capabilities; client never decides authority from flags alone.
risks: Flag debt; flags must not be used as an authorization mechanism.
rationale: Four of five references rely on it; Verevon needs kill switches for agent features in multi-party Spaces.

name: Tray, jump list and taskbar/dock badges
best: slack: Clear three-state icon (rest/unread/highlight) derived from aggregated unreads with a count tooltip and launch-control menu; Teams adds presence-aware icon and a jump list with status changes and "Up next" meetings (teams-shell-and-native-010); buzz shows running agents in the tray (INF, buzz-architecture-102).
mechanism: Aggregate unread/mention counts per workspace -> tray state + tooltip + OS badge; menu built from workspaces and quick actions; refresh on unread or locale change.

verevon.gap: Unread counts exist only inside the navbar; the document title is static ("verevonv3") and no Badging API / favicon badge is used, so a background tab shows nothing.
verevon.strengths: Navbar already has message and notification unread counts to feed a badge.

benefit: Users see Space mentions and finished agent runs without switching tabs; a tray list of running agents makes "agents work like colleagues" tangible.
approach: Now: set document.title "(n) Verevon" and navigator.setAppBadge from the navbar unread counts (S). Later in the shell: tray with unread state and running-agent list fed by Model Plane run status via the gateway.
risks: Badge counts must respect per-Space mute settings.
rationale: The web part (title/app badge) is a few hours of work with immediate user value; the native tray waits for the shell.

name: Window management: placement memory, multi-display healing, custom chrome, close semantics
best: slack: Bounds clamped to a live display work area, DPI healing after dock/undock, title bar themed by the active workspace; Teams adds close prompts for unsent pop-out messages and calls (teams-shell-and-native-013).
mechanism: Persist bounds per window type; validate against screen.getAllDisplays; debounce re-apply scale on display/resume events; WindowCloseAction policy with prompt cases.

verevon.gap: No native windows. Web equivalent of the close prompt (beforeunload on unsent composer text or a running agent) was not verified.

benefit: Mostly shell polish; the "unsent draft / running run" close prompt is the one piece with web value.
approach: With the shell: tauri-plugin-window-state. Web now: beforeunload guard when the Space composer has text.
risks: Over-eager beforeunload prompts annoy users.
rationale: Shell polish.

name: Pop-out windows for chats, channels and calls
best: teams: Window manager with tagged windows, per-type persisted placement, named mutations and docking (q5, 65 endpoints); Slack-shell-and-native-018 shows the safe way to let the web app open native child windows (option allowlist, minimal preload).
mechanism: Window tags (ChatPopout, Meeting, Presenter); open via a bridge call with allowlisted options; each window loads the same SPA route in a compact layout; shared state via the server stream.

verevon.gap: No pop-out found in the Space UI; check whether a Space thread or an agent run console can be opened as a standalone compact route (window.open is used only for search results and OAuth popups).

benefit: Watching an agent work (run console, browser view) in a side window while chatting in the Space is a natural agent-cooperation pattern.
approach: Web first: compact routes (/spaces/:id/thread/:tid?popout=1, /runs/:id?popout=1) opened with window.open; each window has its own SSE subscription; shell later adds placement memory.
risks: Multiple SSE connections per user increase gateway load; consider a SharedWorker multiplexer.
rationale: Teams-only differentiator; valuable for agent watching but not blocking.

name: In-app keyboard shortcuts and command palette
best: grokbot: Every shell action is a registered command (id, hotkey, enabled-in-editor flag) consumed by one hotkey layer and a mod+K palette, including previous/next Bot; Teams adds user-assignable custom shortcuts and a slash menu that doubles as a palette (teams-product-surface-147); qm adds hold-Cmd to reveal 1-9 session shortcuts (qm-architecture-116).
mechanism: Command registry {id, label, hotkey, when, run}; one keydown handler resolves hotkeys (capture phase for global ones); palette fuzzy-searches commands + entities (Spaces, people, agents); custom bindings stored per user.

verevon.gap: Basic keys (tablist roving focus, picker arrows, Enter-to-send) exist, but no quick switcher between Spaces, no command palette (Cmd/Ctrl+K opens web search), no shortcut help or custom bindings.
verevon.strengths: Verevon already has a typed ActionDescriptor registry (id, label, risk, requiresApproval, zod schemas) used by both human clicks and model-initiated actions; a palette can sit on top of it.

benefit: A palette that lists the same typed actions agents can call (with risk/approval badges) gives humans and agents one action vocabulary in a Space, which no reference does; quick switching is table stakes for chat power users.
approach: Frontend: command registry wrapping shared/actions descriptors + navigation commands; Cmd/Ctrl+K = palette (move web search into it as one provider), Cmd/Ctrl+1-9 Space switching, "?" shortcut sheet; execution via ActionCommand preview/approval path so authority stays in the owning plane.
risks: Rebinding Cmd+K changes an existing habit (web search); approval-required actions must never execute directly from the palette.
rationale: 4 of 5 sources have shortcuts and two have palettes; Verevon's action registry makes this a cheap differentiator.

name: OS-wide global shortcuts and push-to-talk
best: slack: Validated registration API for combos and modifier double-presses with key-down/key-up events (enables push-to-talk), plus layout tracking (slack-shell-and-native-045). buzz also binds push-to-talk (buzz-architecture-102, INF).
mechanism: Native global-shortcut registration with validation; key-up events for hold-to-talk; keyboard layout change hook remaps accelerators.

verevon.gap: Not possible in a browser tab; Verevon has a voice feature that would benefit from push-to-talk.

benefit: Push-to-talk to a voice agent from any app; summon an agent quickly.
approach: tauri-plugin-global-shortcut in the shell, routed to the voice feature.
risks: Shortcut collisions with other apps.
rationale: Only with a shell; useful for voice agents.

name: Floating quick composer / command center over any app
best: grokbot: Transparent always-on-top 320x176 panel on all workspaces: click to compose, switch Bots from a menu, drag, unmount; prompt goes to the selected Bot (macOS/Linux only). Slack gates a tray-click "Slackbot Mini" overlay behind a flag (slack-shell-and-native-010).
mechanism: Frameless transparent window loading a minimal composer page with its own preload; typed IPC to submit a prompt to the selected agent; window visible on all workspaces.

verevon.gap: No equivalent; requires a native shell.

benefit: Makes personal agents feel like a colleague one keystroke away; aligned with the Grok Bot reference in Verevon's vision.
approach: Tauri secondary window + global shortcut; posts to the same gateway run endpoint as the Space composer (prompt lands in the user's personal Space so it is auditable).
risks: Prompts typed outside a Space must still carry ZDR and org context.
rationale: Agent-native differentiator, but gated on the shell decision.

name: Theming, high contrast, custom palettes, org branding and density
best: teams: Custom themes with accent colours, high-contrast icon sets, OS theme and text-scale propagation at scale (q5). qm imports iTerm2/VS Code palettes with contrast checks and adapts panes to four density tiers (qm-product-123); buzz derives the whole UI from a code-editor theme (buzz-product-168).
mechanism: Tokens as CSS variables; theme = system|light|dark|contrast; derive palette from a few key colours with contrast enforcement; observe prefers-color-scheme / forced-colors / text scale; org branding (name, accent, mark) from config.

verevon.gap: System/light/dark preference is saved server-side and applied, with an accent colorScheme; no forced-colors/high-contrast handling (grep found no prefers-contrast/forced-colors), no org branding (name/mark/accent per org), no density setting.
verevon.strengths: Theme preference persisted per user on the server (follows the user across devices), dark workroom styling shipped.

benefit: High contrast is an accessibility requirement for enterprise buyers; org branding helps multi-company Spaces show whose space it is.
approach: Add forced-colors media rules for status marks and focus rings; Control Plane org branding fields (accent, mark) surfaced through the navbar payload; density as a CSS variable.
risks: Brand colours with poor contrast; enforce contrast at save time.
rationale: Core theming exists; remaining items are polish except high contrast.

name: Typed, versioned preference store with effective-value view
best: slack: One Joi-validated settings object with four layers and a Settings Editor showing each row's effective value and source; preferences are edited in the web UI and validated again by the shell. grokbot exposes agent-relevant settings (model, schedule time zone, microphone, per-Bot colour) in a zod-versioned file that refuses bad files rather than resetting (grokbot-agent-runtime-080).
mechanism: Schema (zod/serde) with version and migrations; layers default < org policy < user < device; read API returns value + source; writes validated server-side.

verevon.gap: Theme is saved server-side but locale lives in localStorage (verevon.locale), so preferences are split across stores; no layered org-policy vs user view, no per-agent preferences (time zone for scheduled agent work, default model) verified. Check src/features/settings for a unified store.
verevon.strengths: A settings feature area exists and theme follows the user across devices.

benefit: Agents acting for a user need user preferences (time zone, language, model) server-side, not in browser storage; admins need org-policy layering.
approach: Control Plane user/org preference document with schema version and layered resolution; gateway exposes effective values; Model Plane reads time zone/language for agent runs.
risks: Migration of existing localStorage values.
rationale: Useful consolidation; not user-visible on its own.

name: Localization with many locales, ICU plurals and RTL
best: teams: 63 locales with a regional fallback map, app locale independent of OS locale, host notifies the web client on locale/input-language change; grokbot adds RTL and native endonyms in 35 locales (grokbot-agent-runtime-085).
mechanism: Message catalogs keyed by id (Lingui/ICU), plural/select formatting, fallback chain (en-au -> en-gb -> en), dir=rtl on html, Intl for dates in the user locale.

verevon.gap: Two locales via inline tr(no, en) pairs; Space activity grammar labels hard-coded Norwegian and dates forced to nb-NO; no catalog extraction, plurals or third language path.
verevon.strengths: Ahead of buzz and qm (English only): Norwegian-first with English, and a code-keyed bilingual error catalog.

benefit: Correct language for each participant in a mixed Norwegian/English Space; agents' activity lines read naturally; a path to Swedish/Danish markets.
approach: Fix activity grammar and date formatting to use the active locale (S); then move tr() pairs to ICU catalogs keyed by id (e.g. Lingui works with Solid) when a third locale is planned.
risks: Agent-generated text is in the model's language, not the UI locale; pass the viewer locale to the Model Plane.
rationale: The hard-coded Norwegian in activity grammar is a visible bug for English users; full catalogs can wait.

name: Crash, hang and load-failure recovery (error curtain, watchdogs, restore orchestration)
best: teams: Diagnosis-specific error curtain (certificate, proxy auth, policy, damaged package, low memory, outdated WebView) with Restart/Repair/Open on web (q5); Slack's fatal-exception and unresponsive dialogs with telemetry flush (q5); grokbot restores the session as one lifecycle with a 30 s stuck detector reporting the stage reached (grokbot-agent-product-170).
mechanism: Root boundary catches render/chunk-load failures -> curtain with classified cause + actions; watchdog timers on boot stages emit "stuck at stage X" telemetry; hang detection offers wait/reload; safe-mode switches (disable GPU).

verevon.gap: Code comments state the app has zero Suspense/ErrorBoundary and no root ErrorBoundary, so a render exception can blank the whole SPA; no boot watchdog or classified failure screen; per-feature error states (e.g. budget_exceeded in the Space composer) exist.
verevon.strengths: Per-feature typed error states with translated copy.

benefit: A Space left open all day must survive a render bug or a lazy-chunk 404 after deploy; showing "reconnecting / reload" instead of a blank page protects trust in agents working in the background.
approach: Add a root Solid ErrorBoundary per shell region (navbar, Space, side panels) with reload/report actions and chunk-load-error auto-reload; a boot watchdog that records the stage reached (session, navbar, Space projection, SSE) to gateway observability.
risks: Boundaries that swallow errors silently; always report with a request id.
rationale: Small effort, removes a whole-app failure mode in a realtime workroom; every native reference invests heavily here.

name: Coded error registry with retryability
best: grokbot: 108 coded errors (SAND-E0001..E0812) grouped by domain with retryable flags and the code location that raises them (q5).
mechanism: Central registry object {code: {name, domain, retryable, summary, payload, seededFrom}}; UI and telemetry key on the code; retry logic reads retryable.

verevon.gap: The gateway returns {code, message} on every error and the client maps ~100 codes to Norwegian/English copy (plus the ZDR refusal catalogue), but there is no retryable flag, domain grouping or coverage check that every emitted code is catalogued.
verevon.strengths: Code-keyed envelope + bilingual copy + ZDR refusal catalogue is close to the grokbot pattern and better than buzz/qm/slack/teams records show.

benefit: Agents and the UI can decide retry vs ask-the-user from the code; support can search by code.
approach: Extend errors.ts entries with domain and retryable; add a gateway test that every code in envelope::error call sites exists in the catalogue.
risks: Catalogue drift without the coverage test.
rationale: Verevon is most of the way there; small hardening.

name: Diagnostics and support kit (logs, net log, report a problem)
best: slack: Self-service kit (net log, verbose restart, tracing UI, cache reset, installation id) and per-surface rotating logs with zipped upload; Teams adds report-a-problem with screenshots, heap snapshots and chunked upload (teams-shell-and-native-029).
mechanism: Per-window rotating console logs with truncation; one action zips logs + state + ids and uploads to a support endpoint; report-a-problem form attaches recent request/trace ids and an optional screenshot.

verevon.gap: No report-a-problem flow found by name (reportProblem/sendFeedback grep empty); check src/features/support and gateway observability.rs for a user-facing "report this" that attaches request ids.

benefit: "Report this agent run" with the run id, request ids and Space id lets support reproduce agent misbehaviour without screenshots of private content.
approach: Report dialog in the Space and run console that sends ids and client errors (no message bodies by default; respects ZDR) to a Support Plane ticket via the gateway.
risks: Uploading content from ZDR Spaces; default to ids only.
rationale: Agent-heavy collaboration produces hard-to-reproduce issues; ids-only reporting fits ZDR.

name: Enterprise network compatibility: proxies, private CAs, streaming diagnostics
best: grokbot: In-app Network Debugger plus copy that tells IT to allow specific domains and disable SSL inspection/DLP/proxy buffering so HTTP/2, SSE and long connections work; all child processes inherit the system CA and proxy.
mechanism: Connectivity probe classes (DNS, TLS, proxy, stream stall) run against each endpoint; results shown with remediation text; proxy/CA inherited from the OS.

verevon.gap: Browser handles proxy/CA, but Space realtime and agent runs stream over SSE through the gateway; no connectivity self-test or IT guidance was checked. Verify whether the SSE path detects buffering proxies (e.g. heartbeat stall detection).

benefit: Enterprise customers behind buffering proxies otherwise see agent runs "hang"; a self-test turns a support ticket into a checklist.
approach: Gateway /diagnostics/stream endpoint that emits timed heartbeats; client measures stall and shows IT guidance; publish an allowlist document.
risks: Low.
rationale: Cheap insurance for enterprise rollouts of streaming agent UIs.

name: Developer/QA affordances and end-to-end test harness
best: buzz: E2E bridge mocks IPC and relay subscriptions; ~189 Playwright files; review standard requires tests that bind production seams and are falsifiable.
mechanism: Test bridge replaces transport with scripted fixtures; Playwright drives the real UI; dev flags select web sources only when unpackaged or explicitly allowed.

verevon.gap: Playwright configs (incl. a real-authority config) and a product demo mode exist; Space-specific e2e coverage and a mock realtime bridge were not assessed here.
verevon.strengths: Real-authority Playwright config tests against real planes rather than mocks only.

benefit: Developer productivity; keeps Space realtime behaviour verifiable.
approach: Add a scripted SSE fixture for Space events so e2e tests can assert agent activity rendering deterministically.
risks: Mock drift from real contracts.
rationale: Developer-facing; Verevon already has the base.

name: Startup performance: bundled assets, prewarm, code cache, perf telemetry
best: teams: Serves a bundled copy of the web client from disk with a version floor and CDN fallback (q5) and shares scenario marks plus INP-style responsiveness telemetry between shell and web (q5).
mechanism: Intercept static requests and serve local copies keyed by an asset manifest; scenarioStart/Mark/Stop API emitting success/failure/abandoned; long-input-delay events; prewarm expensive engines at idle.

verevon.gap: Not assessed: check vite.config.ts chunking, whether route-level lazy loading is used for Spaces, and whether web-vitals/INP are reported to gateway observability.

benefit: Space open time and composer latency are what users feel; scenario telemetry (open Space -> first event rendered) gives a measurable target.
approach: Web: service-worker app-shell cache (with the PWA), route-level code splitting, web-vitals INP/LCP + custom "space_open" scenario marks sent to gateway observability.
risks: Stale service-worker caches; pair with version gating.
rationale: Worth doing once the PWA exists; no evidence of a current problem.

name: Multi-workspace and multi-account switching with cross-workspace unread
best: teams: One isolated web instance per account/tenant with shared notifications and calling state (guest tenants work side by side); Slack-shell-and-native-040 is the best switching UX (rail, Ctrl/Cmd+1..9, tray, jump list, swipe).
mechanism: Per-account isolated session partitions; an aggregator polls/streams unread per account; switching swaps the active session without re-login.

verevon.gap: Org switching exists (one active org at a time via switchOrganization); no cross-org unread indicator, no simultaneous sessions, no keyboard switching.
verevon.strengths: Server-side active-org switch keeps ACLs per org (no client-side mixing).

benefit: Guests from partner companies (Teams-style external collaboration in Spaces) need to see activity in their home org and the host org without re-switching.
approach: Gateway endpoint returning unread counts for all orgs the user belongs to (each computed under that org's own ACL); org rail with badges; switch remains a server-side active-org change.
risks: Must not leak another org's Space names into the current org context; counts only.
rationale: Real need for cross-company Spaces, but the core switch exists.

name: Desktop sign-in via the system browser (PKCE / device-code handoff)
best: qm: Two-minute single-use code via qm-desktop:// redeemed with an S256 proof key, replay prevented across portal instances, isolated cookie partition per instance; grokbot uses a polling variant (grokbot-agent-runtime-138).
mechanism: App creates verifier+state, opens /auth/desktop?challenge=..; portal mints sealed code bound to challenge/state/audience; deep link returns code; app redeems with verifier for a session cookie in its own partition.

verevon.gap: No desktop client, so no handoff; the web BFF session model is already the right target for it.
verevon.strengths: BFF cookie session means the handoff only has to mint the same cookie.

benefit: Required for any native shell without weakening the BFF model.
approach: Gateway /auth/desktop PKCE endpoint minting the same HttpOnly session in the shell partition; reuse Control Plane identity.
risks: Code interception; keep TTL short and single-use.
rationale: Security-critical part of the shell, not standalone.

name: Authenticated, cacheable media in the client
best: buzz: Custom URI scheme plus loopback proxy that mints a fresh per-request media grant, supports range requests and caches across channel switches; grokbot uses content-addressed avatar files behind a token-guarded protocol.
mechanism: Media URLs point to a local scheme/proxy that adds short-lived authorization and forwards Range headers; cache keyed by content hash.

verevon.gap: Not checked: how Space attachments and avatars are served (likely same-origin through the gateway with the session cookie, which would make the custom-scheme trick unnecessary). Verify Range support and cache headers on the gateway media route.

benefit: Fast, private media in Spaces (screenshots from agent browser sessions, files).
approach: Gateway media route with cookie auth, Range, ETag and private cache-control; signed short-lived URLs only for <video>.
risks: Caching private media on shared machines; honour ZDR (no-store for ZDR Spaces).
rationale: The BFF likely solves most of it; verify.

name: Multi-surface reach: installable PWA, phone layout and mobile apps
best: qm: One web build with a phone mode below 860 px (drawer sidebar, bottom sheets, 44 px targets, composer kept above the keyboard via visualViewport), installable, but no service worker/push. buzz has full native mobile (Flutter, biometrics, badges; buzz-product-166) but its web client cannot chat (buzz-product-167).
mechanism: Shared breakpoint constant for CSS and JS; visualViewport listener for the composer; web app manifest; service worker for app shell + Web Push; Badging API.

verevon.gap: Responsive workroom layout and dark theme ship, but there is no web app manifest, no service worker and no Web Push, so Verevon cannot be installed and cannot notify when the tab is closed; no native mobile app.
verevon.strengths: Single responsive web build already covers phone and desktop browsers (better than buzz, whose web client cannot chat).

benefit: Installable app with push for Space mentions and finished agent runs gives most of Teams/Slack desktop+mobile presence at a fraction of a native shell; agents that work while the user is away need a way to reach the user.
approach: Add manifest (name, icons, display standalone, protocol_handlers, share_target), a minimal service worker (app shell cache + push handler), Web Push subscriptions stored by the Application Plane notifications service and sent per user preference; setAppBadge from unread counts. Push payloads carry ids only (fetch content after open) to respect ZDR.
risks: Stale SW caches; iOS push limits (installed PWAs only); push payloads must not contain message text from ZDR Spaces.
rationale: Highest value-per-effort path to Teams/Slack-level presence; unblocks notifications for agent work done while the user is away.

name: OS signals and permissions (idle, lock, network, screen capture, activity history)
best: teams: Only source: session lock/unlock/suspend, system idle time, network level and display topology exposed to the web client.
mechanism: Native event subscriptions forwarded as host events; idle time polled; permission checks with deep links to OS privacy panes.

verevon.gap: Only document visibility is used (to slow navbar polling when hidden); no idle-based presence (away) and no online/offline handling verified.

benefit: Accurate human presence (active/away) in a Space tells agents and colleagues who is available, which matters for routing approvals to a present human.
approach: Web: visibility + input-idle timer (and Idle Detection API where permitted) feeding presence heartbeats to the Application Plane; navigator.onLine + SSE health for a reconnect banner.
risks: Presence is personal data; make it org-scoped and optional.
rationale: Presence itself belongs to another category; the client signal part is cheap.

name: About, What's New and release notes
best: slack: Only source with a record.
mechanism: Component windows/pages for about and release notes; What's New entry.

verevon.gap: Not checked; no build version is exposed to the client (see version gating).

benefit: Telling users what new agent capabilities they have drives adoption.
approach: Release-notes page fed from the deploy pipeline, shown once per version.
risks: None.
rationale: Low-cost adoption aid.
